newsitem.title: USA: Hayes Micro to deliver 56K modem in January 1997.
newsitem.headline: Hayes Micro to deliver 56K modem in January 1997.

text.p: Hayes Microcomputer Products Inc will begin to deliver 56 kilobit per second modems in January, the company told a press briefing on Friday.
"We will be shipping the 56K modem in January," Marshall Toplansky, Hayes' vice president of marketing, said. Modems are hardware that allows computers to communicate via telephone lines.
The firm noted that all modems in its current Optima, Accura and Century lines have been upgraded to 33.6K.
It said that customers with 28.8K modems will be able to upgrade their units to 33.6K now, and ultimately 56K, by sending the machine back to Hayes for a "chip swap."
The 33.6K upgrade will cost "less than $100," Toplansky said.
The company said prices of the upgrade to 56K and of the new modem itself are not yet available since it has not priced the chips for the unit.

Hayes said the 56K modems will use technology from Rockwell International Corp. Hayes noted that it is working with other modem makers and Internet service providers towards creating an industry standard for the 56K modems.

Hayes introduced the new modem plans as one of the first in a group of products it plans to release by the first quarter on 1997. The firm, newly reorganized after Chapter 11 backruptcy, may launch an initial public offering in about one year, a company executive said.
